cultural.vision_reason: This is a European-style silver pair-cased verge/cylinder coach watch with a Roman-numeral enamel dial, a Western horological complication (rack striking, date indicator) — a design and manufacturing tradition entirely of European (likely English) clockmaking, not an object made or used within Azeri Iranian material culture. No positive evidence ties it to Azeri craftsmanship; it reflects outside manufacture, possibly only later owned or traded in the region.

physical.summary:
SILVER AND JAPANNED PAIR CASED HOUR-STRIKING VERGE COACH WATCH WITH DATE INDICATOR AND ALARM [ESCAPEMENT CONVERTED TO CYLINDER].
:
MOVEMENT
Circular gilt-brass plates with four turned pillars. Gilt-brass barrel with ratchet and click set-up mounted under the front-plate. Fusee with chain and standard stop-work. Four wheel going train now terminating with a cylinder escapement which is a conversion from the original verge. Spiral balance-spring with geared regulation, the silver disc engraved A III-XII R. Silver balance-bridge pierced and engraved with flowers.
:
Rack striking for hours only, driven by a fixed barrel engraved on the visible side. Geared stop-work.
:
Alarm train driven by a fixed barrel. Both alarm and striking trains have adjustable fly-pinion for changing the speed of the hammer. Both trains also have geared stop-work.
:
DIAL & HANDS
White enamel dial with an outer circle of minutes )-60 surrounding Roman hours I-XII. Inner circles 1-31 for the date and 1-12 for alarm setting. Dial signed above and below the centre. Pierced gilt-brass hour and minute hands, polished steel calendar hand and blued steel alarm setting hand. In the dial plate and case band a lever for strike/silent [Schlag/Nicht Schlag].
:
CASES
Silver inner case with pierced foliate panel in the band. Silver swivel pendant.
Vernis Martin covered brass outer case with silver hinge, rims and surrounds to the pierced roundels in the band and bezel. The roundels alternate with double piqué pin decoration.
